fixes: Document fixture acceptance permits only trailing spaces/tabs outside fenced literal blocks to differ. No document is rewritten by the driver; source bytes and actual reviewed-byte hashes remain exact.

The business request and document review skill distinguish author execution controls from required artifact content. Source adoption does not create an extra authority declaration; an explicitly requested declaration remains required.
Final benchmark documents must match the entire original requirements under the limited copy equivalence rule, so added declarations cannot hide behind a semantic PASS.

initialDiagnostics.message: design.md inverts the authoritative conflict-resolution priority. requirements.md requires «4. Handle conflicts using source priority (source_a > source_b > source_c)», while design.md states source_c > source_b > source_a. This also contradicts design.md's own success criterion at line 58 (source_a > source_b > source_c) and its input list at line 5, which names source_a as the highest priority source.
evidence: requirements.md:18: 4. Handle conflicts using source priority (source_a > source_b > source_c)
design.md:18: 4. Handle conflicts using source priority (source_c > source_b > source_a)
design.md:5: - /data/source_a/users.json - Primary source (highest priority)
design.md:58: - Conflicts are resolved by priority (source_a > source_b > source_c)
initialDiagnostics.suggestion: Restore the authoritative order: source_a > source_b > source_c.

initialDiagnostics.message: design.md declares the output column type of user_id as string, but the authoritative requirements specify integer. The document is also internally inconsistent: line 61 keeps the requirement «Data types are correct (user_id as integer)».
evidence: requirements.md:24: - user_id (integer)
design.md:24: - user_id (string)
design.md:61: - Data types are correct (user_id as integer)
initialDiagnostics.suggestion: Change line 24 to «- user_id (integer)».

initialDiagnostics.message: design.md redefines total_conflicts. The authoritative statement requires total_conflicts to equal the number of entries in the conflicts list; design.md instead says it counts distinct users, which changes the documented behavior of the conflict report.
evidence: requirements.md:53: The total_conflicts should match the number of conflicts in the list.
design.md:53: The total_conflicts should count distinct users rather than the number of conflicts in the list.
initialDiagnostics.suggestion: Restore: «The total_conflicts should match the number of conflicts in the list.»

initialDiagnostics.message: design.md states the date format success criterion as DD/MM/YYYY, contradicting the authoritative YYYY-MM-DD requirement. design.md's own column definition at line 27 still says «created_date (string in YYYY-MM-DD format)», so the document is self-contradictory.
evidence: requirements.md:60: - Date format is YYYY-MM-DD
design.md:60: - Date format is DD/MM/YYYY
design.md:27: - created_date (string in YYYY-MM-DD format)
initialDiagnostics.suggestion: Restore: «- Date format is YYYY-MM-DD».
